anti_rescue: After the first Prince/Muse session receives a prepared LIVE-002 packet, do not change the candidate generator, task generator, policy seal, baseline order seed, 16-task schedule, four-selection budget, packet protocol, researcher identity, RunPod provider/SKU/rate contract, runtime target, spend ceilings, pass threshold, available-tool policy, or receiver acceptance rule. Freeze pass, no advantage, disadvantage, budget exhaustion, environment mismatch, protocol failure, or execution failure. Any redesign gets a new experiment ID.
claim_boundary: A pass establishes only observed single-run live selection transfer under this GPU-capable Prince substrate on these fresh receiver-executed microtasks.
Prince may select any four candidates from the same full 12-candidate pool; the receiver independently executes the returned four in order and decides acceptance.
If Prince ignores or reconstructs the presentation order and the inherited advantage disappears, that negative result stands.

GPU availability is a matched researcher tool. Different tool use caused by different presentation order is observed behavior, not an input mismatch, provided the tool contract and limits are identical.
Muse is a fixed shared subscription substrate whose per-session dollar allocation is not observable; LIVE-002 reports that limitation instead of inventing a price.

A pass does not establish Level 4 recursive improvement, recursive self-improvement, live coding productivity, repeatability, universal task-family transfer, production value, economic payback, or hostile-process isolation.
The ordering policy was inherited from prior calibration; it was not generated, independently promoted, and inherited by this live improvement loop, so recursive improvement remains unearned.

design.only_treatment: candidate presentation order from exact frozen evidence ranker versus frozen baseline order
design.researcher_authority: proposal-only selection of four candidate IDs and their evaluation order

live001_terminal_predecessor.carry_forward: Do not reinterpret or resume LIVE-001. LIVE-002 changes only the cost-observability contract and GPU-capable researcher tool substrate under a new experiment ID.

primary_metric.name: paired_receiver_confirmed_success_after_gpu_capable_prince_selects_four_from_full_pool
positive_requires: evidence arm has at least two more receiver-confirmed successes than baseline across 16 paired tasks
evidence arm uses fewer downstream receiver evaluations than baseline
both responses bind to the identical frozen RunPod GPU contract
all GPU runtime/spend telemetry is within the frozen $2.56 total / $1.28 per-arm authorization and runtime stopping rule
no paid external service other than the frozen RunPod GPU is used

question: Does the exact frozen evidence-derived presentation order improve GPU-capable Prince's ability to select receiver-confirmed executable improvements versus the frozen baseline presentation order when every other visible packet input, researcher configuration, GPU contract, available-tool policy, and limit is matched?

resource_accounting.budget_exhaustion_rule: If the frozen RunPod SKU/rate is unavailable, if Prince cannot complete within the runtime limit derived from the $1.20 target, or if any arm would exceed its $1.28 GPU authorization, stop the entire experiment. Do not retry, substitute GPU/provider, add funding, or increase the ceiling.
resource_accounting.gpu_spend_formula: frozen quoted RunPod hourly rate × observed GPU runtime seconds / 3600
